page.title: tinyactors: like SQLite, but for actors
page.description: tinyactors runs every order and every user session as its own statechart inside your process, and tests each one over thousands of simulated runs.

hero.headline: Like SQLite, but for actors
hero.lede: tinyactors runs each order or user session as its own small state machine, a few hundred bytes, inside your program.

section.heading: Write each actor's behavior as one chart
section.p: Each of those state machines is an actor: it keeps its own data and handles one event at a time.
Its behavior is a statechart, written in the W3C's SCXML, so a chart means the same in every runtime.

section.heading: Run millions of actors in your process

claim.statement: It runs on your event loop
claim.p: Your actors run beside the rest of your code, in Node.js, Bun, Python, a browser or C.
That is an actor in Node.js, measured with a million of them in one process.

claim.statement: A sleeping actor keeps about 120 bytes
claim.p: An idle actor waits in your database and wakes on its next event. Each operation costs about the same at four million actors as at two.
claim.source: Each operation at two and four million

section.heading: Hand a chart to a coding agent
section.p: A chart holds an actor's whole behavior, so an agent reads one file instead of tracing calls across a codebase.
The chart sends an event for every effect, and your code performs it. A simulated clock runs its timeouts, so an agent tests each change in milliseconds.

section.heading: Kill your unit tests
section.p: A unit test checks the runs you thought of. A property is a rule that holds on every run a program generates.
Does this payment ever charge a card four times? This program asks a thousand times, with random answers, on a clock that jumps to each timeout:

example.caption: Change attempts < 3 to attempts < 4 in the chart, and seed 10 fails. The whole program is 44 lines.

claim.statement: It passes the W3C's own tests
claim.p: SCXML defines what every transition does, and tinyactors passes all 191 automatic tests of the W3C suite.

section.heading: Build a team chat
section.p: Five steps, each a program you can run, take one room to a thousand users.

item.text: One actor, and a handler for the screens.
Each user is offline, active or away.
One actor decides which rooms exist.
A thousand users, fifty in memory.
Running actors move to their chart's next version and keep the state they reached.
A process holding two million actors copies into a 165 MB snapshot that another process restores.
Each step an actor takes becomes a span in your OpenTelemetry collector.
